section: A Threshold to the Subtle Lights
anchor_text: a sealed letter passes through several trusted hands
caption: Traces the chain of custody by which the inherited sciences pass from the prophets and saints, through the author's sanctioned recording, into the reader's hands as a trust.

section: 1. The Sealed Lamp and the Road Home
anchor_text: Five Suradiqs, each of five chapters
caption: Shows the book's five-fold nested architecture in which each Suradiq contains five chapters and each chapter contains five sections.

section: 2. The God No Pointing Can Reach
caption: Maps the faculties that cannot reach God against the one faculty that does, clarifying the section's central argument.

section: 3. The Sin of Naming the Unnameable
anchor_text: what life is, what knowledge is, what power is, what choice is
caption: Shows the four faculties that make up total knowledge (the knowledge of life) granted to the created intellects.

anchor_text: There are five canopies in all
caption: Shows the book's nested 5×5×5 architecture, where each canopy contains five gates and each gate contains five chapters.

section: 5. The Nearest Rank: Breaking the Self to Climb
anchor_text: Below the ranks proper there are two thresholds you must first cross
caption: Maps the ascent from the two thresholds below the hudud (Mustajib, Mu'min) into the ranks proper, beginning with the Mukathir.

section: 6. Every Teacher a Threshold, Not a God
caption: Traces the Mukathir's ascent as a sequence of ranked stations, each climbed before the next.

section: 6. Every Teacher a Threshold, Not a God
anchor_text: onto a soul already made subtle
caption: Shows how the road first refines the sensory soul, then divine sciences connect to finish and transmute it.

section: 7. Out of Nothing, and Equal in Justice
anchor_text: seven names in all for a single thing
caption: Shows the single originated realm radiating into its seven names, clarifying that the cluster of titles names one reality seen from seven sides rather than seven separate worlds.

section: 7. Out of Nothing, and Equal in Justice
caption: Lays out the three denials that define ibda in its purity: no matter before it, no matter beside it, and no place beneath it.

section: 8. The First to Say There Is No God But He
anchor_text: the whole of Tawhid in its completeness
caption: Shows the single act of declaring oneness resolving into its three doctrinal branches — Tawhid, tanzih, and tajrid — that a later tradition would name and number separately.

section: 8. The First to Say There Is No God But He
anchor_text: By looking at his own essence and at his kind
caption: Traces the sequence by which the first form derives monotheism and is answered — from looking, to knowing, to negating and affirming divinity, to seeking means, to receiving the divine supports.
